Devon: Two Coasts and a Moor

Devon is unique in having two dramatically different coastlines — the rugged, surf-battered north coast facing the Atlantic and the gentler south coast with its palm-lined harbours and red sandstone cliffs. Between them lies Dartmoor, one of England's last true wilderness areas. Together, they create a motorcycle destination of remarkable variety.

The North Devon Coast

The A39 Atlantic Highway follows the north coast from Barnstaple to the Cornish border, passing through Ilfracombe, Combe Martin, and Hartland. The road swoops along the cliffs with views across the Bristol Channel to Wales. Side roads drop to hidden coves and surfing beaches. Lynmouth and Lynton, connected by a Victorian cliff railway, are Devon's most dramatic coastal settlements.

The South Devon Coast

The south coast from Exeter to Plymouth is softer and warmer. The English Riviera (Torquay, Paignton, Brixham) has a Mediterranean feel. Further west, Dartmouth and Salcombe are exquisite harbour towns accessible by narrow lanes. The South Devon AONB coast between Bolt Head and Start Point is one of England's most beautiful stretches.

Dartmoor Connection

Dartmoor sits in the heart of Devon, and every coastal ride can include a moorland detour. The B3212 from Exeter to Yelverton crosses the moor's spine, passing wild ponies, granite tors, and medieval clapper bridges. Two Bridges and Postbridge are good stops for refreshments. The moor is open and exposed — a dramatic contrast to the sheltered coast.

Devon's variety is its strength. You can ride along surf-pounded cliffs in the morning, cross a wild moor at lunchtime, and watch the sunset from a palm-lined harbour in the evening.

Best Devon Stops

  • Lynmouth — Dramatic harbour at the foot of towering cliffs, cream teas and coastal walks
  • Clovelly — Famous steep cobbled village, no cars allowed, donkeys carry goods
  • Dartmouth — Beautiful naval town with castle, estuary views, and fine dining
  • Salcombe — Yachting paradise with sandy beaches and subtropical gardens
  • Widecombe-in-the-Moor — Classic Dartmoor village, famous fair in September

Practical Information

Devon's roads can be narrow with high hedges and blind bends — ride cautiously, especially on the south coast lanes. Fuel is available in all towns but can be scarce on Dartmoor between Moretonhampstead and Tavistock. The climate is mild — Devon rarely sees snow, and spring arrives weeks before the north. Summer traffic can be heavy on the A38 and A380 approaches. Best months for riding: May-June and September.
keyTakeaways: Devon has two contrasting coastlines: the rugged Atlantic north coast and the gentler, warmer south coast.
The A39 Atlantic Highway follows the north coast from Barnstaple to the Cornish border through Ilfracombe and Lynmouth.
The south coast around Dartmouth, Salcombe and the English Riviera has a Mediterranean feel and red sandstone cliffs.
Dartmoor sits in the heart of Devon, and the B3212 across its spine adds a wild moorland detour to any coastal ride.

faq.q: What makes Devon a varied riding destination?
faq.a: Devon is unique in having two dramatically different coastlines. The north coast is rugged and surf-battered, facing the Atlantic, while the south coast is gentler and warmer with palm-lined harbours and red sandstone cliffs. Between them lies Dartmoor, one of England's last true wilderness areas, so you can ride cliffs, moor and harbour in a single day.

faq.q: What is the best road on the north coast?
faq.a: The A39 Atlantic Highway follows the north coast from Barnstaple to the Cornish border, passing through Ilfracombe, Combe Martin and Hartland, swooping along the cliffs with views across the Bristol Channel to Wales. Lynmouth and Lynton, connected by a Victorian cliff railway, are the most dramatic coastal settlements.

faq.q: Can I combine the coast with Dartmoor?
faq.a: Yes, and it is well worth it. The B3212 from Exeter to Yelverton crosses the moor's spine, passing wild ponies, granite tors and medieval clapper bridges, with Two Bridges and Postbridge good stops for refreshments. The open, exposed moor is a dramatic contrast to the sheltered coast.

faq.q: What should I watch for when riding in Devon?
faq.a: Devon's roads can be narrow with high hedges and blind bends, so ride cautiously, especially on the south coast lanes. Fuel is available in all towns but scarce on Dartmoor between Moretonhampstead and Tavistock. Summer traffic can be heavy on the A38 and A380 approaches.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride in Devon?
faq.a: The best months are May-June and September, avoiding the peak summer crowds. Devon's climate is mild, rarely sees snow, and spring arrives weeks before the north, so the riding season is relatively long compared with the Highlands.
